clue.text: Special soldier

blocks.note: first meaning: reserved for one person, not public
second meaning: the lowest rank in the army

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of an elite trooper, but the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for something personal or exclusive and a noun for an ordinary enlisted soldier of the lowest rank.

clue.text: A fruit or two, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is spoken, so the word is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: a pair is a set of two

explanation.surface: Someone is offered one piece of fruit, or maybe two.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is a sweet, juicy tree fruit, narrow at the top.

clue.text: Time to alter story!

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so these letters take a new arrangement

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer decides the moment has come to revise their tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A news item is one report or story in a paper or bulletin.

clue.text: Is Arachne finding Vince friendly?

blocks.note: Arachne is the setter, who refers to herself as I, so 'Is Arachne' becomes AM I
Vince Cable, British Liberal Democrat politician and former Business Secretary

explanation.surface: The setter asks whether she is getting on well with Vince.
explanation.walkthrough: Arachne is the setter's pseudonym, so she is I, and 'Is Arachne' turns into AM I. Vince Cable led the UK Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Amicable means friendly and goodwilled, as in an amicable settlement between parties.

clue.text: Time to muse

blocks.note: an era is a period of time
taken as written

explanation.surface: It is the moment to sit and ponder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb meaning ponder; it is a noun, one of the nine Greek goddesses.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry, one of the nine daughters of Zeus.

clue.text: Tantrums about games

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the word is read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: a strop is a British informal word for a sulk or fit of temper

explanation.surface: Someone throws fits over the games being played.
explanation.walkthrough: A strop is everyday British slang for a bad-tempered sulk.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports are athletic games and contests, so the plural noun matches the plural definition.

clue.text: Equable Pole appearing oddly sarcastic

indicators.note: oddly points at the odd-numbered positions, so only first, third and so on are kept

blocks.note: the first and third letters of the word
acid remarks are biting and sarcastic

explanation.surface: A calm Polish person seems strangely cutting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' seems to qualify sarcastic, but it acts on the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Placid means calm and not easily upset, which is an even, equable temperament.

clue.text: Meteorological events on Mars stir confusion

indicators.note: confusion is disorder, so these letters are jumbled into another order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Weather on the Red Planet causes chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Rainstorms are spells of heavy rain with wind, happenings studied by weather science.

clue.text: Drizzling a bit

blocks.note: first meaning: raining lightly
second meaning: a small scattered amount

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as the weather being slightly wet; the two parts are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprinkling is a verb form for light rain falling and a noun for a small quantity spread thinly.

clue.text: Eric's entertained by a fellow from New York, perhaps

indicators.note: a guest entertained by a host is taken inside their home, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the name taken as written
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Eric is being hosted by a visitor from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks New York as just one example of where such a person could come from.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Yorker is one instance of a citizen of the United States, which the 'perhaps' signals.

clue.text: Comparatively friendly male having a row

blocks.note: M is the standard abbreviation for male
taken as written
a tier is a row, as of seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: A man who is friendlier than others gets into an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' tempts as a quarrel, which clashes with friendly; here it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Matey is British informal for chummy, and its comparative form means more chummy than another.

clue.text: Bogdan skips round Polish city

indicators.note: the two words sit round the city's letters, so they enclose them across the word break

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A Polish man named Bogdan skips around the city.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a Baltic port city in northern Poland, once called Danzig.

clue.text: Former PM ordains who'll be reshuffled

indicators.note: a reshuffle rearranges a cabinet, so these letters are dealt out again in a new order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A former prime minister decides who will be moved in a cabinet reshuffle.
explanation.walkthrough: Harold Wilson was Labour Prime Minister of the UK in the 1960s and 1970s; the reshuffle is apt for a PM.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Wilson led the British government twice, from 1964 to 1970 and 1974 to 1976, so he is a past premier.

clue.text: A horribly fat setter creates a lingering impression

indicators.note: something horribly done is a mess, so these letters come out disordered

blocks.note: taken as written
the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An overweight crossword compiler leaves a bad memory behind.
explanation.definitionFit: An aftertaste is a flavour that stays after eating, and figuratively a feeling that stays after an experience.

clue.text: Call emendation "idiotic"

indicators.note: something idiotic makes no sense, so these letters are put into a sensible order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone labels a correction to their text as stupid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Call' reads as describe something as; it is the definition, meaning to name.
explanation.definitionFit: To denominate is to give a name to or designate, which is what calling something means.

clue.text: Self-indulgent, having generous income

blocks.note: free with something means generous with it
a living is the income one earns

explanation.surface: A person with a big salary lives indulgently.
explanation.definitionFit: Free-living describes someone who gives in to their pleasures, which is being self-indulgent.

clue.text: Victor loves to make love — it's magic!

blocks.note: Victor is V in the NATO alphabet
love is zero in tennis, so two loves are two Os
to do something is to make it
love is a score of nothing, O

explanation.surface: Victor enjoys romance, and calls it enchanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is a religion of Caribbean origin associated with sorcery, so by extension it means magic.

clue.text: Boswell regularly is a creature of the night

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so every second letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of the name

explanation.surface: James Boswell, Johnson's biographer, is said to keep late hours.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal birds of prey, active and hunting after dark.

clue.text: Spanish town is short of a herb

indicators.note: something short is lacking its end, so the last letter of the word is cut

blocks.note: Tarragona is a city in Catalonia, Spain

explanation.surface: A town in Spain lacks a particular herb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short of' reads as lacking; here short alone trims the town name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarragon is an aromatic herb with narrow leaves, used in French cooking and sauces.

clue.text: Perhaps having no sense of self-importance

blocks.note: e.g., for example, signals that something is perhaps one case
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A modest person perhaps lacks any conceit.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as having no conceit, but the definition is the conceit itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego in everyday use means an inflated view of one's own worth, a sense of self-importance.

clue.text: Moron lacks potential to be a swimmer

indicators.note: potential is what something could become, so these letters may be remade into something else

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: An idiot has no hope of making it as a competitive swimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swimmer' suggests a person; it is a fish. Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish, sold in fish and chip shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a trade name for dogfish or similar fish, and a fish is a swimmer.

clue.text: Sweet, rich chap's extremely eligible

indicators.note: at the extremes means at either end, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: a toff is British slang for a rich, upper-class man
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A charming wealthy man is a highly eligible bachelor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' reads as an adjective praising the chap; it is a noun, a confection. A toff is a posh, upper-class Brit.
explanation.definitionFit: Toffee is a chewy confection made from boiled sugar and butter, so it is a sweet.

clue.text: Changing to more trying branch of maths

indicators.note: changing something alters its form, so these letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A student switches to a harder area of mathematics.
explanation.definitionFit: Trigonometry is the part of mathematics dealing with the angles and sides of triangles.

clue.text: Strict former partner has to do something

blocks.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
to act is to do something

explanation.surface: A stern ex-spouse must take action.
explanation.definitionFit: Exact describes something precise and rigorous, allowing no deviation, which is strict.

clue.text: Father's anger

blocks.note: the S of the possessive taken as written
ire is anger

explanation.surface: Dad's temper flares.
explanation.walkthrough: The possessive S doubles as a letter of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sire is to father offspring, and a sire is the male parent, especially of an animal.

clue.text: Cut salaries for a long time

indicators.note: cutting removes a piece, here the head of the word

blocks.note: wages are pay, salaries

explanation.surface: Pay has been reduced for a lengthy period.
explanation.definitionFit: Ages is an informal way of saying a very long while, as in I waited for ages.

clue.text: They support County

blocks.note: first meaning: poles or sticks used to lean on
second meaning: the short form of Staffordshire, an English county

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like fans backing a County football side. Staffs is the standard abbreviation for Staffordshire, a county in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking staffs hold people up, and Staffs is the usual shortened name of the English county of Staffordshire.

clue.text: Good sport is tall and awkward

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
angling, fishing with rod and line, is a sport

explanation.surface: A good sportsman is lanky and clumsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangling describes someone lanky and loose-limbed, moving without grace.

clue.text: Team taking part in genteel event

indicators.note: something taking part in an event sits inside it, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A side plays in a refined sporting occasion, cricket perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket and football teams have eleven players, so a side is called an eleven.

clue.text: Offers to supply vehicles

blocks.note: first meaning: formal bids to do work or supply goods
second meaning: boats or rail wagons that carry stores or fuel for a larger vessel or engine

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as bids to provide cars; the plural noun serves both meanings separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenders are formal bids, and also the small boats or coal wagons that serve ships and steam locomotives with provisions.
